Twins Ausar and Amen Thompson are now the first pair of brothers in NBA history to each receive a $100 million deal. They have signed for a total of $363 million this offseason.

Thompson lands the fully guaranteed extension after finishing third place in the Defensive Player of the Year award race last season, leading the NBA in steals per game and posting the third-most combined steals and blocks at 215. He is one of three players with at least 300 steals and 150 blocks since entering the NBA as the No. 5 pick in the 2023 draft.
Just in: Detroit Pistons All-Defensive forward Ausar Thompson has reached agreement on a five-year, $155 million rookie-scale contract extension, sources tell ESPN.
Heat, Pelle Larsson agree to 4-year, $60M extension - via @ESPN App https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49975177/heat-pelle-larsson-agree-4-year-60m-extension

The Heat are set to have a major rotation role for Larsson, who averaged 11.4 points per game last season, up nearly 7 points per game from his rookie season. He also ranked fourth-best in offensive efficiency in Miami, per ESPN Research, and fifth in minutes played.

Larsson has become a foundation piece for the Heat amid their offseason overhaul after being a second-round find in the 2024 draft, and now two seasons into his career the 6-foot-5 guard avoids restricted free agency next summer and locks in a new deal with a mutual option that fully guarantees $60 million while allowing either side to opt-in on 2030.
Miami Heat guard Pelle Larsson has agreed to a new four-year, $60 million contract extension, with a mutual option for the 2030-31 season, Austin Brown and Steven Heumann of CAA Sports tell ESPN.

The Denver Nuggets are signing 2023 first-round pick Cam Whitmore on a two-way NBA deal, sources tell ESPN. Whitmore enters his fourth NBA season after averaging 10.5 points and 3.3 rebounds over 119 career games -- and has already joined the Nuggets for workouts in Denver.

Give the Thompson parents their flowers 🌹 

Ausar Thompson just secured the bag, agreeing to a five-year, $155 million rookie-scale contract extension with the Pistons. 

But this massive deal is about way more than just one player. 

It cements his entire family in the NBA record books.

With Ausar's payday, he and his twin brother, Amen, are now in a league of their own. 

They are the first pair of brothers in NBA history to each receive a contract worth over $100 million 💵 

Because Amen recently inked a massive five-year, $208 million extension with the Rockets, the twins have now signed for a combined $363 million just this offseason alone. 

Securing that kind of generational wealth at the exact same time is completely unprecedented.

You also have to give a massive shoutout to their parents. 

Raising one NBA player is incredibly rare, but raising two elite, lottery picks who both secure max-level money is a completely different level of success. 

They did an amazing job helping them reach the absolute peak of the sport.

Massive congratulations to the entire Thompson family on a life-changing summer.
